LESSON: HANDLING WASTE MATERIALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Materials
Topic 3.2: Handling waste materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Handling waste materials, part of Materials in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can we reuse waste materials?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to handling waste materials in the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Handling waste materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. Identify waste materials found in the environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Handling waste materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe ways of handling waste materials safely in the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Handling waste materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. recycle waste materials to make items for day-to-day use, e) appreciate the need for proper waste management in the immediate environment. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to watch captioned/signed video clips or observe a demonstration on how to sign terms related to handling material in the immediate environment. • In pairs, learners are guide to fingerspell and sign terms related to handling waste materials in the immediate environment. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to visit a nearby market within the locality to identify waste materials. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Handling waste materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy: effective communication skills are developed as the learner searches for information on safe ways of

handling waste materials in the environment

• Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices to search for information

on safe ways of handling waste materials in the environment.

31

Value:

Responsibility: learner safely handles and disposes waste materials when making household items from waste materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Internet Safety and Security: responsible online behaviour is enhanced as learner uses digital or print resources to search for

information on safe ways of handling waste materials.

Link to other subjects

Creative Arts: learner enhances design skills when making items from recyclable waste materials.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print media.

• Digital devices.

• Personal protective equipment (PPEs)

• Plastic, glass, metal, paper, electronic waste, animal waste, construction waste
